group_assessment.weighting: Retrospective multicentre Brazilian cohort of 40 patients (36 families) with pathogenic or likely pathogenic SLC2A1 variants, clinical data by teleconsultation or visit, a new unvalidated severity score, ketogenic therapy in 85%. It is a disease-class comparator (brain glucose transport failure treated by glucose-sparing diet), not a dextrose or fluid study and not WWOX. Several internal numerical inconsistencies limit how far its figures can be quoted.

entries.proposition: The cohort is 40 patients from 36 families, mostly children (median age 9.1 years), collected by teleconsultation in 32 and retrospective review.
entries.snippet: Detailed information on family history, abnormal pre‐ and perinatal events, age at onset of seizures, psychomotor development, age at diagnosis, and response to treatment provided were collected and retrospectively reviewed.

entries.proposition: 85% were on ketogenic dietary therapy (27 classic, 7 modified Atkins).
entries.snippet: Thirty‐four patients were on a ketogenic diet (85%).
entries.anchor: Results, Ketogenic Diet and Severity Assessment

entries.proposition: Seizure control exclusively with the ketogenic diet was reported in 11 patients (31.4%) in one paragraph and 21 patients (56.7%) 'relying exclusively' on it in the next; the denominators differ and are not reconciled.
entries.snippet: In 11 patients (31.4%), seizure control was achieved exclusively with the ketogenic diet.
entries.anchor: Results, Ketogenic Diet and Severity Assessment

entries.proposition: Twenty-one patients (56.7%) used the diet exclusively for seizure management.
entries.snippet: Overall, 21 patients (56.7%) relied exclusively on a ketogenic diet for seizure management
entries.anchor: Results, Ketogenic Diet and Severity Assessment, second paragraph

entries.proposition: Diet-only patients had lower severity scores than patients also on drugs; severity and treatment choice are confounded, so this is not a diet effect.
entries.snippet: The median Glut1‐CSS was 7 [IQR: 2–10] for the first group, compared to 13 [IQR: 11.25–15.75] for the latter 2 groups.
entries.anchor: Results, Ketogenic Diet and Severity Assessment

entries.proposition: Reported adverse effects of the diet were constipation, irritability and nausea, transient at the start; the Introduction says it is well tolerated with hardly any side effects.
entries.snippet: The most common were constipation (28.5%), irritability (8.5%), and nausea (5.7%).
entries.anchor: Results, Ketogenic Diet and Severity Assessment

entries.proposition: The authors say the severity scale is their own and not externally validated.
entries.snippet: This modified scale is not yet externally validated and should be considered an exploratory phenotypic stratification tool.

entries.proposition: Table 3 gives patient 28 a language score of 6 although the scale for that domain stops at 5, so the table contains an out-of-range value.
The missense severity split is reported as 60%, 30% and 20%, which sums to 110%.
entries.snippet: Patients with missense variants more frequently exhibited a mild phenotype (60% mild, 30% moderate, and 20% severe)

entries.proposition: CSF glucose is reported in the body only for one individual (low); the 10-patient CSF statement exists only in the abstract, which is not an evidentiary surface here.
entries.snippet: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed hypoglycorrhachia in the boy.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 table gives the mild-group current age as 7.0 [5-9.55] whereas the text gives [5.18-9.73]; seizure-free time, diet start and duration medians agree with the text.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 1 table: mild current age 7.0 [5-9.55], moderate 10.0 [6.8-25], severe 11.8 [7.8-13.6]; seizure onset 0.5, 0.2, 0.2 years; seizure-free time 2.0, 3.7, 0.2 years; diet start age 3.6, 5.0, 5.0; time on diet 2.85, 4.15, 1.85 years.

experimental_context.system: Brazilian Glut1-DS cohort, n = 40, by Glut1-CSS stratum
experimental_context.endpoint: medians of age and diet variables

entries.proposition: The authors conclude that the ketogenic diet was associated with improvement, that complete seizure freedom occurred only in a subset, and name the retrospective design as the main limitation.
entries.snippet: Although ketogenic diet therapy was associated with clinical improvement in seizure frequency and neurodevelopmental trajectory, particularly when introduced early, complete seizure freedom was achieved in only a subset of patients.

entries.proposition: The main limitation named is the retrospective design.
entries.snippet: The main limitation of our study concerns the retrospective design, which may have introduced registration bias and hindered the standardization of clinical assessments.
